breaks.note: CBI redefined base money from Esfand 1399: its foreign assets were revalued and the IMF's 2016 Monetary and Financial Statistics Manual classification was adopted (footnote 1 of the monthly tables). A month is on the revised definition only where an edition printed it so, and growth is not computed across the two definitions; each month carries its method.

notes: Source: Central Bank of Iran, Selected Economic Indicators (monthly Excel editions from Tir 1399, three months per edition, so monthly levels from Tir 1398), and CBI's tsdview time-series history for quarter-end months before that.
Every value is an END-OF-MONTH STOCK in thousand billion rial (هزار میلیارد ریال), exactly as CBI publishes it; ÷10 gives همت (trillion toman). It is not a monthly average.

Growth: m/m against the previous month, y/y against the same month a year earlier, and since-Esfand against the previous Esfand, all by Jalali month. The annual headline is Esfand over Esfand, as CBI reports it; the annual average needs all twelve months.
About 2.7 points of 1400's liquidity growth come only from Mehr Eqtesad bank's figures being added to Sepah's; CBI states this has no monetary effect, and growth is still computed across it.
CBI marks its newest base-money figure as fully preliminary (کاملا مقدماتی); it is revised in later editions more often than liquidity is.

data_age.note: CBI states no release date. Its monthly workbooks have arrived 21 to 164 days after the month they describe (three weeks to five and a half months, measured from the workbooks' own last-saved times), often several at once. age_days is measured from the end of the newest stored month to today (Tehran); that month is called stale after 195 days, the longest lag plus one month, because until the next month is published the newest stored one is a month older than it.
